script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Tuesday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed six point nine one percent up on the session.

Marvell Technology surged twelve point eight zero percent on Tuesday. That is the single largest gain across all ten primary holdings. The move demands attention, and the catalyst is not fully priced in yet.

Stocks broadly ripped higher on Tuesday. Two forces drove the move: stronger-than-expected earnings across multiple sectors, and a sharp drop in oil prices following reported progress in United States and Iran diplomatic talks, which eased geopolitical risk premium across markets. The Nasdaq powered to new highs, the S&P five hundred also closed at record territory, and risk appetite was firmly in control throughout the session.

The top story on Tuesday belongs to Advanced Micro Devices. The company reported second quarter earnings after the close, and the headline numbers were strong — revenue climbed fifty percent year over year, and the data center segment more than doubled, posting one hundred and seven percent growth against the same quarter last year. The company also delivered a third quarter outlook that beat analyst estimates. And yet, the stock dropped in after-hours trading. That gap between strong fundamentals and negative post-earnings price action tells you something important: the bar was simply set too high. Analysts at multiple outlets noted that investors needed more than a modest beat to justify current valuations. The position held its Tuesday gains, but the after-hours pressure is worth monitoring closely heading into Wednesday's open.

Advanced Micro Devices was up seven point zero zero percent on the session. As noted, the earnings release brought a fifty percent revenue surge and data center sales doubling year over year, but the after-hours reaction turned negative as the quarterly beat was characterized as modest relative to elevated expectations. Watch Wednesday's open carefully — the gap between Tuesday's close and after-hours levels will be the first signal.

Micron Technology was up seven point six two percent on Tuesday. Bank of America reiterated its buy rating and a price target that reflects strong conviction, calling the recent pullback an enhanced buying opportunity as cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure demand remains solidly on track. Separately, Micron debuted a new artificial intelligence storage platform in partnership with Microchip Technology, adding a product catalyst to the macro tailwind. The next signal to watch is any further analyst commentary on memory demand trends.

NVIDIA was up two point five six percent on Tuesday. That is the softest gain among all ten primary holdings on a day when the broader semiconductor complex moved aggressively higher. The broader market rally, driven by earnings strength and oil's decline, provided general lift, but NVIDIA notably lagged its peers. Watch whether that relative underperformance persists or normalizes on Wednesday.

Broadcom was up six point six one percent on the session. No specific company news drove the move — the gain tracks cleanly with the broader semiconductor rally and reflects the group's continued leverage to artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Upcoming earnings from the sector remain the next key catalyst.

Intel was up ten point eight four percent on Tuesday. That is the second-largest gain in the portfolio on the session, a notable move for a name that has faced persistent structural headwinds. No single company-specific headline drove the surge, suggesting short-covering and sector momentum were primary forces. Execution on its foundry roadmap remains the longer-term watch item.

Applied Materials was up five point four eight percent on the session. The equipment sector broadly participated in Tuesday's risk-on move. No specific news, but semiconductor equipment names tend to track wafer fabrication demand expectations closely. Earnings and capital expenditure guidance from major chipmakers remain the key forward driver.

KLA Corporation was up six point nine five percent on Tuesday. Like Applied Materials, the move reflects sector-wide strength rather than a standalone catalyst. The inspection and process control equipment market remains tied to leading-edge node investment cycles. Watch for any commentary from foundry customers on capital spending plans.

Marvell Technology was up twelve point eight zero percent — the strongest single-session gain in the portfolio on Tuesday. No specific news item was identified as the direct catalyst, making the magnitude of the move even more notable. The stock's leverage to custom artificial intelligence silicon and data center connectivity has kept institutional interest elevated. Watch for any company-specific announcements or analyst upgrades in the sessions ahead.

Lam Research was up seven point eight five percent on the session. The deposition and etch equipment leader moved in lockstep with the broader semiconductor equipment complex. No company-specific news was the driver. Lam's revenue sensitivity to memory capital expenditure cycles ties it closely to Micron's trajectory — Tuesday's Micron news is relevant context here as well.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was up two point seven two percent on Tuesday. Like NVIDIA, it was among the more modest gainers in the portfolio on a strong sector day. As the world's leading contract chipmaker, its revenue exposure spans nearly every name in this portfolio. Any forward guidance commentary from major customers will carry weight.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Advanced Micro Devices' Wednesday opening print — after-hours pressure following earnings means the gap open will set the tone for the position. Second, any Federal Reserve speaker appearances scheduled mid-week that could shift rate expectations and re-price growth assets. Third, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's next monthly revenue data — any deviation from trend directly affects the entire semiconductor supply chain.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Wednesday's Advanced Micro Devices open is the number one price event to watch.
